method: Forecut editorial forecasts synthesise public Indian designer interviews, international SS27 show notes, textile-trade coverage and brand collections. Runway presence is not sell-through. Lifecycle labels are qualitative development priorities, not measured market shares. 2028 entries are conditional scenarios; no 2028 runway or sales evidence is claimed. Palettes are original Forecut working colours, not an official colour authority forecast. Festival groupings are merchandising windows, not verified religious dates; Eid timing requires a separate calendar check.

sources.title: FDCI · Kunal Rawal, India Couture Week 2026

sources.title: Hermès · Women’s spring-summer 2027

sources.title: Première Vision · SS27 fabric decoding
sources.note: Public trade coverage supports light natural blends, fluid shirting, textured weaves and sheer layers. Supplier availability must be verified.

sources.title: Première Vision · AW27–28 season overview
sources.note: Public textile-fair overview puts material development at the centre. Used as a long-lead input, not as a reproduced proprietary forecast.

sources.title: ANOKHI · Summer 2026, Kambaya
sources.note: Indian brand reference for mud-resist, indigo and restrained handmade detailing. A prior-season retail offer, not a 2027 collection.

Summer 27.title: Air, craft and ease
Summer 27.basis: Near-term forecast · medium directional confidence; product demand unmeasured
Summer 27.focus: Build around breathable separates, fluid drapes and light craft. Reserve sheer, playful and experimental surfaces for small capsules rather than making them the whole range.

themes.title: Cloth before decoration
themes.story: Summer comfort is the starting point. Develop tactile cotton, linen and fine woven sets whose value comes from handle, proportion and finish.
themes.products: Straight kurta with relaxed trousers; linen overshirt; handloom shirt dress; lightweight everyday saree.
themes.make: Compare unlined and half-lined samples. Test shrinkage, opacity, seam slippage and hand feel after laundering. Avoid heavy fusible panels that defeat airflow.
themes.commercial: Protect easy-care core styles; introduce higher-cost handloom in a tightly edited premium capsule. Validate supplier lead times before range sign-off.

themes.title: Light, with coverage
themes.story: Sheer runway layers become wearable when opacity is designed into the garment. The Indian opportunity is a light overlay with an intentional inner, not an exposed look copied from a show.
themes.products: Organza over cotton-silk; airy cape over a day lehenga; fluid dupatta; sleeveless inner with a loose shirt.
themes.make: Specify inner length, armhole coverage and attachment points. Check snagging, perspiration marks and movement in daylight.
themes.commercial: Offer the inner as part of the product; keep the outer usable with existing wardrobe pieces. Test colour and size demand before widening.

themes.title: Playful craft, controlled scale
themes.story: Use handwork as a recognisable small detail, with clear maker attribution. Current designer and brand references support experimentation without establishing a universal trend.
themes.products: Contrast hand-stitched pockets; crochet-edge shirts; indigo printed co-ords; small patchwork panels.
themes.make: Keep high-labour detailing away from seams and alteration points. Approve print registration, wash fastness and repeatable stitch quality.
themes.commercial: Create one recognisable craft code across apparel and a small accessory. Replenish the simpler version if the test performs.

themes.title: Occasionwear that moves
themes.story: Bring festive dressing into summer through less bulk and more flexible styling. Practical menswear construction is a relevant Indian lead signal.
themes.products: Light embroidered kurta sets; draped skirt separates; a soft Nehru layer; rewearable wedding-guest lehenga.
themes.make: Use lighter linings, practical pockets and secure drape fastenings. Fit seated, walking and with raised arms; check trim abrasion.
themes.commercial: Sell separates with two styling options. Keep ornate pieces in depth-limited occasion drops and compare returns against simpler sets.

categories: Womenswear
Prioritise light kurta separates, easy sarees and day-function layers. Test a covered sheer capsule; keep fitted statement bodices selective.
Menswear
Develop linen and cotton-silk kurtas, soft jackets and straight trousers. Comfort construction should be visible in the product explanation.
Fusion & western
Use fluid shirts, relaxed sets and craft accents. Build travel versatility through pockets and adjustable styling rather than excess utility trims.
Footwear
Develop padded flats and flexible occasion shoes. Wide-fit grading, rub testing and outsole grip are essential; no demand uplift is assumed.
Textiles & trims
Cotton, linen blends, light handloom and restrained embroidery lead development. Specify composition, weight and care; do not call a fabric sustainable without proof.
plan: October–November 2026
Set customer, occasion and price architecture; source fabric and make first silhouettes.
December 2026
Approve washed fit samples, colour fastness, opacity and costing; book craft capacity.
January–February 2027
Complete pilot production, product photography and size checks; phase deliveries by climate and occasion.
March–July 2027
Review actual full-price sales, returns and replenishment weekly; do not confuse social engagement with purchase.
watch: Confirm Holi and Eid drop timing separately; lunar dates can shift.
Look for repeated lighter construction across Indian SS27 shows, not one standout look.
Stop a sheer or handwork option if opacity, care or quality complaints exceed your own benchmark.

Festive 27.title: Craft with a second life
Festive 27.basis: Forward forecast · medium-low directional confidence; recheck against 2027 Indian shows
Festive 27.focus: Plan festive capsules around lighter embellishment, adaptable separates and rich textile character. Treat sculptural metallic work as an experimental premium edge rather than a volume assumption.

themes.title: Textile becomes the occasion
themes.story: Use the weave and placement of craft to create festive identity. The 2026 couture inputs support fresh treatments of familiar techniques, not a claim that every heritage craft is accelerating.
themes.products: Tonal brocade jackets; fine Bandhani drapes; textured silk kurta sets; narrow-border sarees.
themes.make: Approve handloom yardage early. Align motif placement across sizes and price embroidery by actual labour hours.
themes.commercial: Pair one statement textile with simpler coordinates. Separate cloth-led premium options from entry-price print interpretations.

themes.title: Rewear the celebration
themes.story: Design wedding-guest pieces to be useful after the event. Lighter construction and modular styling are Forecut development recommendations anchored in current Indian occasionwear practice.
themes.products: Lehenga with a wearable separate blouse; detachable cape; reversible waistcoat; light occasion skirt with pockets.
themes.make: Make fastenings accessible, include alteration allowance and test pocket distortion. Photograph both dressed-up and everyday combinations.
themes.commercial: Use bundles and separate purchasing to improve outfit flexibility. Test attach rates before multiplying accessory SKUs.

themes.title: Light as ornament
themes.story: Material reflection can deliver impact with fewer all-over trims. Reflective couture is a premium signal with substantial weight, repair and sourcing risks.
themes.products: Small pearl-effect borders; metallic-cord accents; controlled tissue panels; a statement brooch.
themes.make: Sample skin contact, sharp edges, tarnishing and storage. Offer repair guidance and keep non-washable components removable where possible.
themes.commercial: Keep fragile or expensive surfaces made-to-order or in limited capsules. Never equate couture visibility with volume readiness.

themes.title: Menswear, engineered for the event
themes.story: Combine Indian textile knowledge with movement and personal styling. Regional weather and event format matter more than a single national festive uniform.
themes.products: Soft bandhgalas; tonal embroidered overshirts; secure draped stoles; straight trousers under layered kurtas.
themes.make: Fit across body types and test long seated wear. Consider breathable linings and secure internal fasteners without replicating a designer’s proprietary mechanism.
themes.commercial: Merchandise by event and climate. Offer lighter wedding-guest options beside more elaborate groom pieces.

categories: Womenswear
Build saree, blouse and occasion-skirt combinations. Balance craft visibility with weight, alteration access and repeat wear.
Menswear
Focus on tonal texture and comfortable layering; reserve velvet for appropriate winter markets and venues.
Fusion & western
Test occasion jackets over familiar separates. Keep dramatic drapes proportionate and fastening instructions clear.
Footwear
Pair embellished juttis with simpler padded alternatives; run flex, adhesion, grip and long-wear trials.
Textiles & trims
Book tissue, silk blends and artisan embroidery early. Confirm material origin, repairability and actual production capacity before scaling.
plan: January–March 2027
Revalidate against Indian runway and brand launches; approve regional assortment and supplier capacity.
April–May 2027
Finalise craft strike-offs, fit, wearer trials and cost; retain a fallback fabric for long-lead styles.
June–July 2027
Deliver early Rakhi and Onam capsules; stage later festival inventory by verified dates.
August–December 2027
Reorder proven shapes. Compare full-price sales, return reasons and repeat purchases by region and event.
watch: Recheck couture and textile signals in 2027 before bulk orders.
Track whether buyers choose lighter sets at equal prices; there is no sell-through dataset behind this forecast.
Test one reflective surface first; discontinue unsafe, heavy or unrepairable options.

Summer 28.title: An adaptable summer wardrobe
Summer 28.basis: Long-range scenario · low confidence; not observed 2028 runway evidence
Summer 28.focus: Explore fewer, more useful pieces: breathable modular sets, repair-friendly construction and identifiable local craft. These are conditional development scenarios to revisit when 2027–28 signals arrive.

themes.title: Adaptable summer sets
themes.story: Scenario: versatility becomes a stronger reason to buy if shoppers want fewer occasion-specific pieces. Airy and adjustable 2027 runway ideas are an early design input only.
themes.products: Shirt-and-trouser sets; adjustable wrap kurtas; removable sleeve layers; compact travel capsules.
themes.make: Prototype two ways to wear each piece without excess hardware. Fit-test adjustability at both ends of the size range.
themes.commercial: Run a small paid pilot before committing capacity. Compare conversion and repeat wear feedback with fixed styles.

themes.title: Repair is part of the product
themes.story: Scenario: dependable aftercare helps distinguish premium craft. It depends on service economics and customer adoption, neither of which is established for 2028.
themes.products: Replaceable buttons and ties; spare trim kits; accessible seams; detachable occasion panels.
themes.make: Document repair steps and stock compatible components. Test that removable trims still survive normal wear.
themes.commercial: Cost the service separately before promising it. Measure repair use, lead time and margin impact in a pilot.

themes.title: Craft with a clear origin
themes.story: Scenario: customers reward specific provenance over broad craft language. Local making is an identity cue, not automatic proof of lower impact.
themes.products: Cluster-attributed handloom shirts; small-batch indigo sets; restrained crochet and embroidery accents.
themes.make: Record fibre composition, supplier and process; check batch consistency and substantiate any environmental claim.
themes.commercial: Test product descriptions that explain maker and technique. Validate willingness to pay rather than assuming a premium.

themes.title: Soft structure for daily dressing
themes.story: Scenario: summer tailoring stays relaxed while becoming more purposeful. Build recognisable shapes with better finishing instead of adding novelty to every style.
themes.products: Unstructured overshirts; fluid sarees; straight-leg trousers; breathable waistcoats.
themes.make: Check drape, collar recovery, seam stability and opacity. Build wear trials into development before range expansion.
themes.commercial: Retain a familiar core and trial one silhouette change at a time. Use actual return reasons to set revisions.

categories: Womenswear
Scenario focus: flexible kurta sets, light everyday sarees and detachable occasion layers. Confirm appetite through 2027 customer tests.
Menswear
Scenario focus: unstructured layers and purposeful adjustment; keep dependable straight silhouettes as the comparison group.
Fusion & western
Scenario focus: wardrobe-compatible sets with a small craft signature, rather than speculative microtrends.
Footwear
Explore repairable components and comfortable lasts only with supplier trials; no 2028 sneaker adoption claim is made.
Textiles & trims
Trial traceable blends, repair components and lighter constructions. Availability, certifications and wash performance must precede volume booking.
plan: April–September 2027
Recheck SS28 trade and runway inputs as they become available; revise or reject these scenarios.
October–December 2027
Run customer pilots, aftercare costing and fit trials; lock only validated materials and silhouettes.
January–February 2028
Approve production against verified quality, demand and festival calendar.
March–July 2028
Track sales and returns against the pilot baseline; update scenarios with measured evidence.
watch: A scenario advances only after repeated brand signals and customer testing.
If modular details raise defects or returns, simplify the construction.
Review SS28 collections when published; this report does not describe shows that have not happened.

Festive 28.title: Celebration, built to keep
Festive 28.basis: Long-range scenario · low confidence; review before any commercial commitment
Festive 28.focus: Explore occasionwear whose value comes from reconfiguration, provenance and aftercare. This is an original Forecut planning scenario, not a claim about confirmed 2028 consumer preferences or designer collections.

themes.title: The occasion wardrobe, recomposed
themes.story: Scenario: an existing saree, skirt or kurta gains new life through a fresh layer. Current modular and lighter-occasion inputs support prototyping, not a prediction of guaranteed uptake.
themes.products: Detachable draped panels; separate capes; reversible occasion jackets; mixable saree blouses.
themes.make: Make attachment points discreet and stress-test them. Check fit when parts are used independently.
themes.commercial: Pilot a wardrobe-refresh capsule beside complete looks. Compare attachment sales with unsold component stock.

themes.title: Heirloom surfaces, modern placement
themes.story: Scenario: restrained craft placement makes premium pieces easier to wear again. Heritage should be credited rather than reduced to a generic luxury claim.
themes.products: Narrow woven borders; tonal Bandhani; placed Kantha-inspired handwork through the appropriate maker partnership.
themes.make: Approve stitch density and motif placement on actual size sets. Build traceability and artisan payment into sourcing briefs.
themes.commercial: Test one craft family across a limited range. Validate lead times and gross margin after handwork and finishing costs.

themes.title: Repairable occasion shine
themes.story: Scenario: aftercare becomes part of the premium proposition. Reflective couture offers a visual reference but creates particular durability and storage challenges.
themes.products: Replaceable decorative panels; removable brooches; controlled metallic accents; spare embellished patches.
themes.make: Test abrasion, humidity exposure, trim replacement and packing. Supply a realistic care card and repair route.
themes.commercial: Keep experimental materials in made-to-order or limited runs. Expand only after repair and defect costs are understood.

themes.title: Local making, contemporary shape
themes.story: Scenario: recognisable local techniques pair with contemporary separates. The opportunity depends on supply reliability and demonstrated customer interest.
themes.products: Light craft jackets; textured straight kurtas; draped skirts with pockets; simple occasion footwear.
themes.make: Obtain material and process records. Fit-test for movement and avoid unsupported recycled, regenerative or biodegradable claims.
themes.commercial: Use pre-orders or small pilots to learn about demand. Revisit the range after 2027 and 2028 Indian shows.

categories: Womenswear
Explore reconfigurable saree and skirt outfits and placed craft. Avoid extending today’s trend curve automatically into 2028.
Menswear
Explore contemporary jackets, draped accessories and comfortable occasion trousers; test regional temperature needs.
Fusion & western
Explore component-led occasion capsules that work with existing wardrobe basics. Validate mix-and-match fit and styling clarity.
Footwear
Explore repair-friendly occasion flats and removable decorative elements where safe; wear and snag testing come first.
Textiles & trims
Prioritise verifiable origin and repeatable quality. Keep novel material development conditional on testing and commercial supply.
plan: July–December 2027
Check Indian couture, festive retail and trade-fair developments; replace unsupported scenarios.
January–March 2028
Validate target customers, price tolerance and suppliers; approve initial prototypes.
April–July 2028
Run wear, repair and quality tests; lock only proven options and verified festival delivery windows.
August–December 2028
Monitor sell-through and returns by event and region; record which hypotheses actually performed.
watch: Do not use 2026 couture as proof of 2028 mass-market adoption.
Stop material experiments when safe care or repair cannot be offered.
Replace this scenario with direct 2028 evidence as it becomes available; next planned research checkpoint: July 2027.
